line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Be3
teaches: When a bishop comes out to stare at the knight sitting in the middle, the answer is to reinforce that knight rather than to move it. A defended centre piece cannot be traded profitably, and the defending bishop lands on a square where it will be useful for the rest of the game anyway.
explains: The bishop steps to e3 backing up the knight on d4, so the pressure down the diagonal has nothing to win. Both sides now have a bishop staring at a defended piece, which is a standoff the better-developed side is happy with.
